title: Federal Judge Blocks Trump's Latest Attempt to Limit Birthright Citizenship
detail: US District Judge Deborah Boardman (District of Maryland) ruled Wednesday, September 3, 2026, that Trump's August executive order narrowing birthright citizenship — targeting children born to 'alien enemy' parents or foreign embassy workers — 'is almost certainly unconstitutional,' preliminarily enjoining its enforcement nationwide. In her 35-page ruling, Boardman cited the Supreme Court's June 2026 decision that had already blocked Trump's broader January 2025 birthright citizenship order, writing the president 'has tried, through Executive Order, to upend our country's longstanding tradition of birthright citizenship.' Attorney General Todd Blanche said the ruling 'is not something that is a surprise to us' and vowed the administration would 'continue to fight,' potentially returning to the Supreme Court. Agencies may still draft implementation guidance but cannot enforce the narrower policy.

media.caption: A federal judge blocked Trump's latest executive order narrowing birthright citizenship, citing the Supreme Court's June ruling

title: Lutnick Apologizes After Falsely Claiming No Americans Died in Iran War; Trump Warns of More Strikes 'Anytime We Want'
detail: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick apologized Thursday, September 3, 2026, after telling CNBC's 'Squawk Box' a day earlier that 'there haven't been American deaths' in the Iran war, calling it 'really just an economic chokeout.' In fact 18 US service members have died and more than 750 have been wounded since the US first struck Iran in February. President Trump pre-empted the controversy with a Truth Social post saying Lutnick 'had Venezuela on his mind when he said nobody was killed. 18 people were killed in Iran!'; Lutnick followed roughly 45 minutes later with his own apology, saying he had confused the Iran war with the earlier Venezuela operation, in which no US troops died. The flap came as Trump, following the CENTCOM strikes on Strait of Hormuz radar sites, warned the US was prepared to hit Iran again 'anytime we want,' with Iran's health ministry putting the latest strike death toll at 18, including victims of a strike on a wedding party in Kuhestak.

media.caption: Trump warns US is prepared to strike Iran again 'anytime we want' as Lutnick apologizes for misstating US war deaths

title: Foreign-Born Population Falls 2.9 Million Since Trump Took Office, First Sustained Decline Since 1930s
detail: A Center for Immigration Studies analysis of Census Bureau household survey data, released Thursday, September 3, 2026, found the total US foreign-born population fell 2.9 million from January 2025 (53.3 million) to July 2026 (50.5 million) — the illegal immigrant population accounting for most of the drop, an estimated 2.3 million decline from 15.8 million to 13.5 million, while the legal immigrant population fell roughly 600,000. CIS research director Steven Camarota called it the first sustained net decrease in US migration since the 1930s, reversing an 8.3 million increase during the post-COVID border surge under the Biden administration. CIS attributed the decline to border enforcement and interior removals; the Current Population Survey underlying the estimate covers about 60,000 households and carries a margin of error of roughly ±1 million.

media.caption: CIS analysis finds the US foreign-born population fell by 2.9 million since Trump took office, driven mainly by illegal immigration decline

title: Hasidic Rabbis Meet Trump at White House, Reportedly Seek Help Shielding Yeshiva Students From IDF Draft
detail: A delegation of Hasidic rabbis met with President Trump at the White House on Thursday, September 3, 2026. Hebrew-language media reported the delegation had drafted a letter asking Trump to intervene on behalf of ultra-Orthodox yeshiva students seeking to avoid conscription into the Israel Defense Forces, though the letter was reportedly withheld at the last moment. The meeting adds an unusual data point to Trump's engagement with Israeli domestic politics, where the ultra-Orthodox draft-exemption fight has repeatedly threatened to collapse Prime Minister Netanyahu's governing coalition.

media.caption: Hasidic rabbis met with President Trump at the White House, reportedly seeking help for yeshiva students facing IDF conscription
